headline: The clap test now lands its taps it can prove
lede: The Gauntlet ±50 ms audio/frames acceptance line flaked red whenever the box ran busy. It ships fixed: the harness no longer aims its synthetic tap at the wall clock and hopes — it aims at the instant the game itself stamps the press as banked, and verifies it.

notes.text: Close-loop press aiming (PR #2246, closes #2136): each A-tap dispatches pre-compensated, is verified against a game-side bank stamp, and the residual feeds forward to the next tap. Landing accuracy went from a blind ±60–100 ms to ±15 ms.

The aim was anchored at the wrong clock zero — synth-mic creation vs the recorder's markStart. The gap between those (12 ms cool, 100+ ms hot) had been hiding in every clap offset since the gate was born.

Two physics terms remain on saturated boxes and are filed honestly as #2247: transient input-delivery spikes, and the one-per-second tick clock chording across stall/catch-up staircases. The fix is stamping the clock from audio content time — the audit's 2026-11-12 densify experiment had answered the wrong question.
The mutant stays red by construction: a planted 500 ms desync can never be laundered green by the compensation clamp — alignment is still exactly what the gate grades.

look.text: Gauntlet — its recording gate is what got the new alignment proof
